title: Time: Where dt Comes From, and Which Clock to Ask

questions.question: Which clock should be used to measure how long something took?
options: Either, they behave the same way
system_clock, because it is the actual time
Whichever has the finer resolution
steady_clock, because it never goes backwards and never jumps
questions.explanation: system_clock can be set by an administrator or stepped by a time synchronisation daemon. Elapsed time measured with it can come out negative.

questions.question: What is system_clock actually for?
options: Recording when something happened, for a log or a timestamp a person reads
Measuring intervals precisely
Timing loops that run for more than a second
Nothing, it is obsolete
questions.explanation: A robot uses both clocks in the same program: the steady one for durations, the wall clock for saying when. Swapping their jobs is the bug.

questions.question: What does the chrono library give you that a double named timeout does not?
options: The units live in the type
Automatic thread safety
A smaller memory footprint
Better precision
questions.explanation: Seconds cannot be passed where milliseconds are expected. Confusing milliseconds with seconds is a thousandfold error. With a plain number the units live in a comment, and the mistake is silent.

questions.question: Why does the first tick report a dt of zero rather than the clock's reading?
options: Because the clock has not been initialised yet
There is no previous reading to subtract, and the clock's origin is arbitrary
Because the first interval is always too short to matter
To make the controller start smoothly
questions.explanation: A steady clock counts from a point that means nothing on its own. Reporting it would make a controller integrate a value unrelated to the loop.

questions.question: Why must the clock be injected rather than read directly inside the timer?
options: Because steady_clock is slow to call
To support multiple threads
Otherwise testing two seconds of behaviour takes two seconds, and a backwards step cannot be arranged at all
Because the standard forbids calling now in a class
questions.explanation: With an injected clock the suite covers hours of behaviour in microseconds and can arrange a clock step on demand. It is the same seam as the fake sensor.

questions.question: A loop stalls and dt arrives as three seconds. What should a controller do?
options: Stop the robot immediately
Treat it as zero
Clamp it to a maximum and record that it happened, rather than integrating it
Integrate it, since that is the time that really passed
questions.explanation: Integrating a stall produces one large sudden correction, which on hardware is a lurch. Clamping must be a deliberate decision, which is why it is reported rather than done silently.
